Like his older brother, fellow NBA player [[Tyus Jones]], he played [[college basketball]] for the [[Duke Blue Devils men's basketball|Duke Blue Devils]]. ==Early life== Jones played high school basketball for [[Apple Valley High School (Minnesota)|Apple Valley High School]] in [[Apple Valley, Minnesota]].{{cite web |last=Jones |first=Ryan |title=Tre Jones Is Prepared To Become The Latest Member Of His Family To Orchestrate The Offense At Duke |url=https://www.slamonline.com/college-hs/high-school/tre-jones-duke/ |website=[[Slam (magazine)|Slam]] |access-date=February 7, 2019 |date=April 12, 2018}} He joined the varsity team while in eighth grade and became a starter in his next season.{{cite web |last=Shaughnessy |first=Mike |title=Tre Jones is in the pipeline to Duke |url=https://www.hometownsource.com/sun_thisweek/sports/tre-jones-is-in-the-pipeline-to-duke/article_1ebb6544-a8e8-5ef1-a826-fa3132a12b9e.html |website=Hometown Source |access-date=February 7, 2019 |date=August 14, 2017}} Jones led Apple Valley to two Minnesota 4A state titles, in 2015 and 2017, and averaged 23.5 points, 10.4 rebounds and 7.5 assists in the 2016–17 season.{{cite web |title=Tre Jones |url=http://www.goduke.com/ViewArticle.dbml?DB_OEM_ID=4200&ATCLID=211767529 |publisher=Duke Athletics |access-date=February 7, 2019}} Jones left as a two-time Minnesota [[Gatorade Player of the Year awards|Gatorade Player of the Year]] and earned [[McDonald's All-American Game|McDonald's All-American]] and [[Minnesota Mr. Basketball]] honors after his senior season.{{cite web |last=Caron |first=Emily |title=Point Guard Tre Jones Set to Take the Reins of Duke's Reloaded Offense |url=https://www.si.com/college-basketball/2018/08/24/duke-blue-devils-recruiting-tre-jones |website=[[Sports Illustrated]] |access-date=February 7, 2019 |date=August 24, 2018}}{{cite web |last=Frederick |first=Jace |title=Tre Jones wins 2018 Minnesota Mr. Basketball award |url=https://www.twincities.com/2018/03/28/tre-jones-wins-2018-minnesota-mr-basketball-award/ |website=[[Twin Cities Pioneer Press]] |access-date=February 7, 2019 |date=March 28, 2018}} By the end of his high school career, he was considered a five-star [[college recruiting|recruit]] and one of the best [[point guard]]s in the 2018 class.{{cite web |last=Frederick |first=Jace |title=Is Apple Valley's Tre Jones the nation's best point guard? He sure looks like it. |url=https://www.twincities.com/2017/07/28/is-apple-valleys-tre-jones-the-nations-best-point-guard-hes-certainly-starting-to-look-like-it/ |website=[[Twin Cities Pioneer Press]] |access-date=February 7, 2019 |date=July 28, 2017}} On August 13, 2017, he committed to play college basketball for Duke.{{cite web |last=Parrish |first=Gary |title=Five-star point guard Tre Jones commits to Mike Krzyzewski's Duke Blue Devils |url=https://www.cbssports.com/college-basketball/news/five-star-point-guard-tre-jones-commits-to-mike-krzyzewskis-duke-blue-devils/ |work=[[CBS Sports]] overall = 14 | espn overall = 17 | accessdate = June 4, 2018 | bball = yes }} ==College career== ===Freshman season (2018–19)=== Jones made his college debut for Duke on November 6, 2018, chipping in 6 points, 4 rebounds and 7 assists in a 118–84 win over [[Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball|Kentucky]] at the [[Champions Classic]].{{cite web |last=Mizutani |first=Dane |title=Tyus Jones attends little brother's Duke debut — with an assist from Jimmy Butler |url=https://www.twincities.com/2018/11/07/tyus-jones-attends-little-brothers-duke-debut-with-an-assist-from-jimmy-butler/ |website=[[Twin Cities Pioneer Press]] |access-date=February 7, 2019 |date=November 7, 2018}} On December 20, he led his team to a 69–58 victory over [[2018–19 Texas Tech Red Raiders basketball team|Texas Tech]], collecting 13 points, 5 rebounds, 5 assists and 6 steals.{{cite web |last=Watson |first=John |title=Tre Jones Leads Duke Past Texas Tech And Into 2019 |url=https://247sports.com/college/duke/LongFormArticle/TAKEAWAYS-Tre-Jones-Leads-Duke-Past-Texas-Tech-And-Into-2019--126711321/#126711321_2 |publisher=[[247Sports.com|247Sports]] |access-date=February 7, 2019 |date=December 21, 2018}} Jones suffered a shoulder injury on January 14, 2019, during a collision with Frank Howard of [[2018–19 Syracuse Orange men's basketball team|Syracuse]].{{cite web |last=McCreart |first=Joedy |title=No. 1 Duke loses most irreplaceable player -- guard Tre Jones |url=http://www.startribune.com/no-1-duke-loses-most-irreplaceable-player-guard-tre-jones/504379222/ |website=[[Star Tribune]] |publisher=[[Associated Press]] |access-date=February 7, 2019 |date=January 16, 2019}} He missed two games with the injury and returned on January 26 versus [[2018–19 Georgia Tech Yellow Jackets men's basketball team|Georgia Tech]].{{cite web |title=Tre Jones returns to Duke lineup after two-game absence |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/25849642 |publisher=[[ESPN]] |access-date=February 7, 2019 |date=January 26, 2019}} In his freshman season at Duke, Jones averaged 9.4 points, 5.3 assists and 3.8 rebounds per game in 36 games for the Blue Devils.{{Cite web |title=Tre Jones College Stats |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cbb/players/tre-jones-1.html |access-date=2025-12-07 |website=College Basketball at Sports-Reference.com |language=en}} ===Sophomore season (2019–20)=== On April 8, 2019, it was announced Jones would return to Duke for the [[2019–20 Duke Blue Devils men's basketball team|2019–20 season]].{{Cite news |last=Borzello |first=Jeff |date=April 8, 2019 |title=Duke freshman Tre Jones to return next season |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/26473243 |access-date=April 8, 2018 |work=[[ESPN]]}} He scored 15 points in his sophomore debut, a 68–66 win over [[2019–20 Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball team|Kansas]].{{cite news |title=No. 4 Duke edges third-ranked Kansas 68-66 |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401168155 |access-date=November 5, 2019 |work=[[ESPN]] |agency=[[Associated Press]] |date=November 5, 2019}} Jones had a career-high 31 points in a 74–63 win over [[2019–20 Georgia State Panthers men's basketball team|Georgia State]] on November 15.{{cite news |title=Jones scores 31, No. 2 Duke beats Georgia State, 74–63 |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401168183 |access-date=December 24, 2019 |work=[[ESPN]] |agency=[[Associated Press]] |date=November 15, 2019}} Jones missed games against [[2019–20 Wofford Terriers men's basketball team|Wofford]] and [[2019–20 Brown Bears men's basketball team|Brown]] in late December with a mild foot injury.{{cite news |last=Rowe |first=Adam |title=Coach K updates Tre Jones injury status |url=https://247sports.com/college/duke/Article/tre-jones-foot-injury-duke-blue-devils-mild-sprain-140898142/ |access-date=December 24, 2019 |work=247 Sports |date=December 20, 2019}}{{cite news |last=Medcalf |first=Myron |title=Duke's Tre Jones misses second game with foot sprain |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/28382207 |access-date=December 29, 2019 |work=[[ESPN]] |date=December 28, 2019}} At the conclusion of the regular season, Jones was named ACC Player of the Year and Defensive Player of the Year.{{cite web|url=https://theacc.com/news/2020/3/8/athlete-awards-2020-acc-mens-basketball-award-winners-announced.aspx|title=2020 ACC Men's Basketball Award Winners Announced|website=theacc.com|publisher=Atlantic Coast Conference|date=March 9, 2020|access-date=March 9, 2020}} Jones averaged 16.2 points, 6.4 assists, 4.2 rebounds and 1.8 steals per game as a sophomore.{{cite news |last=Dauster |first=Rob |title=NBC Sports College Basketball All-American Teams |url=https://collegebasketball.nbcsports.com/2020/03/10/college-basketball-all-american-teams/ |access-date=March 16, 2020 |work=[[NBC Sports]] |date=March 10, 2020}} After the season, Jones declared for the [[2020 NBA draft]].{{cite news |last=Wojnarowski |first=Adrian |author-link=Adrian Wojnarowski |date=March 21, 2020 |title=Duke's Tre Jones to enter NBA draft |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/28935276 |access-date=March 21, 2020 |work=[[ESPN]]}} ==Professional career== ===San Antonio / Austin Spurs (2020–2025)=== Jones was selected by the [[San Antonio Spurs]] with the 41st pick overall in the [[2020 NBA draft]] which was hosted on November 18, 2020.{{cite web|title=Spurs select Devin Vassell and Tre Jones in 2020 NBA Draft|url=https://www.nba.com/spurs/spurs-select-devin-vassell-and-tre-jones-2020-nba-draft|date=November 19, 2020|website=NBA.com|access-date=November 19, 2020}} On November 27, Jones signed with the Spurs.{{cite web|title=Spurs sign 2020 second round pick Tre Jones|url=https://www.nba.com/spurs/news/spurs-sign-2020-second-round-pick-tre-jones|date=November 27, 2020|website=NBA.com|access-date=November 27, 2020}} On February 1, 2021, Jones received his first assignment at [[G League]].{{cite web|title=San Antonio assigns Tre Jones to Austin Spurs|url=https://austin.gleague.nba.com/news/san-antonio-assigns-tre-jones-to-austin-spurs|date=February 1, 2021|website=NBA.com|access-date=February 1, 2021}} On March 17, 2023, his brother [[Tyus Jones|Tyus]] got his first [[triple-double]], against Tre, when San Antonio lost in overtime to the [[2022–23 Memphis Grizzlies season|Memphis Grizzlies]], but just 16 days later Tre matched his brother's triple-double count with 17 points, 11 assists and 10 rebounds of his own in an overtime win against the [[2022–23 Sacramento Kings season|Sacramento Kings]].{{cite web|url=https://www.si.com/college/duke/nba-blue-devils/duke-basketball-jones-brother-triple-double-4-23|title=Duke basketball alum Tre Jones catches brother in triple-double count|accessdate=April 9, 2023|date=April 3, 2023|work=[[Sports Illustrated]]|last=Giles, Matt}}{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap/_/gameId/401469325|title=McDermott scores 30 to lead Spurs past Kings 142-134|accessdate=April 9, 2023|date=April 2, 2023|publisher=[[ESPN]]|agency=[[Associated Press]]}} On July 8, 2023, Jones re-signed with the Spurs on a two-year, $19 million contract.{{cite web|first=P.|last=Shirley|title=Spurs Re-Sign Tre Jones|url=https://www.nba.com/spurs/news/spurs-re-sign-tre-jones|website=NBA.com|date=July 18, 2023|access-date=September 10, 2023}} ===Chicago Bulls (2025–present)=== On February 3, 2025, Jones, alongside [[Zach Collins]], [[Kevin Huerter]] and a 2025 first-round pick, was traded to the [[Chicago Bulls]] in a three team deal, in which they sent [[Zach LaVine]], [[Sidy Cissoko]], three first-round picks and two second-round picks to the [[Sacramento Kings]], who sent [[De'Aaron Fox]] and [[Jordan McLaughlin]] to San Antonio.{{cite web|title=Bulls acquire Kevin Huerter, Zach Collins and Tre Jones in three-team deal|url=https://www.nba.com/bulls/news/bulls-acquire-kevin-huerter-zach-collins-and-tre-jones-in-three-team-deal|website=NBA.com|date=February 3, 2025|access-date=February 3, 2025}} On June 30, 2025, Jones agreed to a three-year, $24 million contract to return to the Bulls.{{cite web |last=Collier |first=Jamal |date=July 1, 2025 |title=Sources: Tre Jones returning to Bulls on 3-year, $24M deal |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/45622494 |access-date=August 12, 2025 |publisher=ESPN}} ==National team career== Jones played for the [[United States men's national under-17 basketball team|United States]] at the [[2015 FIBA Americas Under-16 Championship]] in [[Argentina]], winning the gold medal. He recorded 19 steals in the competition, breaking the American under-16 record set by [[Malik Newman]] in 2013.{{cite web |last=Rayno |first=Amelia |title=Tre Jones has the look and the motivation of older brother Tyus |url=http://www.startribune.com/tre-jones-has-the-look-and-the-motivation-of-older-brother-tyus/309330701/ |website=[[Star Tribune]] |access-date=February 7, 2019 |date=June 23,
